answer: Newcomers dock at a public jetty and earn nothing until they climb a ledge of verified work. Each of six milestones is a fresh, time-boxed task: a real job fragment finished within an hour, impossible to precompute or outsource in bulk. A random peer re-runs one in three milestones; any failure drops the identity to the bottom ledge and burns its escrowed pay, like light through a prism splitting one claim into many checks. A farm of 100 fakes needs 600 live one-hour tasks, a third re-checked, so scaling means paying for 600 hours of labour per wave.
